text:
morgan: Heads-up — after the 03/02 deploy I'm seeing a reproducible perf regression on mixed-precision runs (FP8/INT8 paths). Throughput down ~18% on our long-continuous workloads, p99 latency +30ms. Continuous-batcher turned on. Anyone else?

li: saw a few alerts this morning, didn't dig in yet. What model and workload?

morgan: gpt-medium-v2 (served with auto-quant-routing). Workload has many short prefixes + long continuations (prefixes ~8-24 tokens, continuations up to 512). Enabled kvcache + continuous batching. Regression appears only when calib-profile mode hits — i.e., when runtime switches kernels based on calibration thresholds.

jamal: curious if kernel selector is thrashing between fp8 and int8 kernels per-batch because batching mixes shapes. Continuous batching packs dissimilar sequences which can push shapes into different kernel buckets. That could force different kernel launches and extra transforms.

perf-bot: profiling snapshot attached (summary): total_kernel_time +21%, memcpys +14%, kernel_launches +29% vs baseline. Hotspots: mixed_matmul_fp8, pack_kv_sgather, pad_and_align_copy.

li: can you paste the perf-bot snippet?

perf-bot: ```
HOT: mixed_matmul_fp8  45.2ms (+28%)
HOT: mixed_matmul_int8 12.1ms (+5%)
WARN: pack_kv_sgather  9.8ms (+60%)
WARN: pad_and_align_copy 7.6ms (+40%)
kernel_launches: 412 -> 532 (+29%)
```

sara: pack_kv_sgather spike is interesting — suggests kvcache layout expectations mismatch with quant kernels (maybe alignment/stride). If FP8 kernels expect packed 128B-aligned KV chunks but continuous batcher produces variety, we could be doing extra gather+repack per-request.

morgan: I tried a quick experiment toggling continuous-batcher -> batcher-fixed: regression goes away. So continuous packing is the trigger. Hypothesis: continuous batcher coalesces short prefixes with long comers; kernel selector sees the batched shape variance and picks FP8 for some partitions and INT8 for others, causing per-micro-batch kernel switches and repacking.

alec: another angle — calibration thresholds changed in last deploy (rounding heuristics for activations). If calibration nudges a layer from int8->fp8 for some sequence lengths, that will change weight packing and kernel layout. Combine that with continuous-batcher mixing different seq_len groups and you get churn.

jamal: can we reproduce with a synthetic driver? Idea: two groups A(short pref length 12) and B(long pref 128), continuous-batcher merging them to same GPU batch. Run with /without new calibration to see kernel selection logs.

morgan: I ran synthetic. Repro steps below:
1) driver: 1000 reqs, 60% group A (seq 12->64), 40% group B (seq 128->512)
2) continuous-batcher enabled, kvcache ON
3) compare baseline-calib (old thresholds) vs new-calib (deployed)

Results: new-calib: kernel_launches +34%, fp8_matmul kernel runs increased 2.7x for some layers, pack_kv_sgather time +2.3x, overall tokens/s -19%. Baseline-calib didn't show that.

li: can you paste kernel selector logs? Even short ones like layer X: chosen kernel=fp8_shaped(64x128) vs int8_shaped(128x128).

morgan: pasted snippet:```
[2026-03-02 09:10:12] layer=attn_7 selector: batch_shape=(31,128) pref_group=short -> kernel=fp8_shaped(32x128)
[2026-03-02 09:10:12] layer=attn_7 selector: batch_shape=(7,512) pref_group=long -> kernel=int8_shaped(64x512)
[2026-03-02 09:10:12] continuous_batcher: merged groups -> actual_launches=3 (fp8_shaped, int8_shaped, fp8_shaped)
```

alec: that log line shows mixed kernel launches for the same layer within one batch — probably because continuous batcher splits the batch internally and the runtime schedules separate kernel calls for each sub-shape. The issue is that the runtime currently doesn't amortize repacking cost across mixed precision subcalls.

jamal: mitigation ideas (short-term):
- add a heuristic to kernel selector: prefer INT8 when mixing will cause >X extra kernel launches (i.e., avoid fp8 unless clear win)
- enforce small sequence length thresholds: any seq_len < 32 forcibly use int8 kernels to avoid pack overhead
- coalesce KV layout early: do a unified pack pass that creates packing for both fp8/int8 variants to avoid repeated memcpys (expensive)

li: long-term: adjust continuous-batcher to maintain micro-batches by precision type (i.e., group by expected kernel if known). That reduces kernel churn and pack/gather repetition.

morgan: I prototyped heuristic #1 on branch morgan/kernelselect-fallback: if continuous-batcher detects >2 precision-switches within a batch, fallback to stable_int8 path for that batch. Quick results: tokens/s recovered +12% vs new-calib but still -6% vs baseline. p99 improved by 18ms.

perf-bot: quick perf comparison (tokens/s)
baseline-calib: 847 tokens/s
new-calib: 685 tokens/s
morgan/fallback-heuristic: 766 tokens/s
```

sara: that's promising. Can we make the heuristic less aggressive? Maybe compute estimated extra bytes copied and estimated kernel overhead to make a cost model, rather than a hard count.

alec: agree. We already have telemetry: avg pack cost per kernel, avg kernel latency per shape. Use those to predict cost of mixed kernels and choose lowest-cost precision for whole batch. This avoids magic thresholds.

jamal: also check KV cache physical layout: maybe we can change the slab allocator to prefer alignment compatible with both fp8/int8 packs to reduce pack_kv_sgather. Small change to allocator might drop that memcpy spike a lot.

morgan: did a micro-alloc experiment: forcing kvcache slab alignment to 128 bytes reduced pack_kv_sgather by ~55% and recovered an extra +6% tokens/s on top of heuristic.

li: summary / action items:
- jamal: prototype batch-level cost-model in kernel selector (P0 for perf sprint)
- alec: change slab allocator to 128B alignment and run regression suite (P1)
- morgan: keep fallback-heuristic as kill-switch for canary envs; add telemetry to measure false-positives (P0)
- sara: small experiment to pre-pack KV for both precisions and measure overhead (P2)

morgan: opened PR with fallback heuristic + telemetry: #4217 (WIP). tagging @jamal @alec for follow-ups.

jamal: I'll start on cost-model tomorrow. If we get a good estimator we can remove the fallback.

alec: will run slab alignment tests on dedicated infra and post numbers. If that helps a lot we might push quick deployment.

morgan: thanks all. will keep thread updated — next step is to validate canary with fallback enabled for a day. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: note: added regression ticket PERF-3912 and flagged canary for 03/04 02:00 UTC.
